turn.user_message: Discharge delays. Our patients are medically fit by mid-morning but most don’t leave till late afternoon.
turn.context: Discharge sample conversation, turn 1 (playbook §1: check how the work really runs before proposing anything).

transcript.label: Sample conversation · turn 1 · walk the road

text: Before I suggest anything, I want to see how discharge really runs at your hospital. Most delays that look like discharge problems start further up the road.
First stop, the doctors. Who writes the discharge summary, who checks it, and who signs it? And when do rounds finish on your busiest wards?
chat.pointer: The whole road is drawn as rooms on one path. Tap any room to see what I will ask there.
chat.note: Most delays start long before the billing desk.

points.label: The doctors: who writes, checks and signs
Nurses: when they count used supplies

prompts: A junior doctor writes it, the consultant signs

blocks.title: The road to going home
blocks.deck: Eleven stops, each run by a different team. We walk them one at a time.

sheets.title: The doctors
sheets.text: The summary is drafted, checked and signed by different people. The round decides when any of it can start.
sheets.entry: Who writes, checks and signs the summary?
sheets.entry_hint: Type a rough answer. It goes into your message.

sheets.title: Supply count
sheets.text: The bill cannot be finished until nurses count the used supplies. They count only when they are free.
sheets.entry: How long after signing do nurses start counting?
sheets.entry_hint: Type a rough answer. It goes into your message.

sheets.title: Pharmacy returns
sheets.text: What was given, what was used and what goes back. Counted by hand, it means a second pass on the bill.
sheets.entry: Who works out the medicines going back?
sheets.entry_hint: Type a rough answer. It goes into your message.

sheets.title: Billing
sheets.text: A charge that arrives after the bill is closed opens it again.
sheets.entry: How many bills were reopened last month?
sheets.entry_hint: Type a rough answer. It goes into your message.

sheets.title: Insurance desk
sheets.text: The insurer’s approval sits inside the family’s wait.
sheets.entry: Does your discharge time include the insurance wait?
sheets.entry_hint: Type a rough answer. It goes into your message.

sheets.title: Bed desk
sheets.text: Discharge times can only be checked against when beds were given out.
sheets.entry: Can the bed desk say when beds were given?
sheets.entry_hint: Type a rough answer. It goes into your message.

sheets.title: Housekeeping
sheets.text: A bed is cleaned from when housekeeping hears, not from when the patient left.
sheets.entry: How long until housekeeping hears a bed is free?
sheets.entry_hint: Type a rough answer. It goes into your message.

sheets.title: Transport
sheets.text: Porters are shared with admissions and scans, at the same busy hour.
sheets.entry: How many porters work at the busy hour?
sheets.entry_hint: Type a rough answer. It goes into your message.

sheets.title: Operating theatre
sheets.text: A bed freed late cannot be used for an operation that same day.
sheets.entry: What is the latest a freed bed helps?
sheets.entry_hint: Type a rough answer. It goes into your message.

sheets.title: Last checks
sheets.text: The dietitian, the pharmacist and the nurse must each see the patient, in no set order.
sheets.entry: Who must see the patient before they leave?
sheets.entry_hint: Type a rough answer. It goes into your message.

sheets.title: Cash counter
sheets.text: Every patient going home meets one counter, in the same two hours.
sheets.entry: Who can let a patient go with money owed?
sheets.entry_hint: Type a rough answer. It goes into your message.

blocks.caption: Each stop is a team. The question in each room is the one I will ask when we get there.
